title: Bounce or Stick? Collisions Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
A cricket bat hits a ball, two marbles click, wet clay hits a wall and sticks. Every one is a collision, but some bounce back and some just stick. On his study table, Aarav's carrom striker sends a coin flying, while a small clay ball just stays stuck to it. Where did the bounce go? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 5, Work, Energy and Power) we learn elastic and inelastic collisions, for NCERT, CBSE, ISC and PUC students, with JEE Main and NEET practice.

Two carts crash three times on a live track, with spring, soft rubber and sticky bumpers. The readout and live bars show the total momentum staying at 12 kg m/s every time, while the graph of total kinetic energy shows 24 J kept, 19.5 J left and 18 J left. A slow-mo replay freezes the biggest squash, where both carts share 3 m/s and 6 J sits in the bumpers. We write the rules step by step: momentum conserved in every collision, kinetic energy kept only in elastic ones, and one shared speed when the bodies stick. Side by side cards compare the striker and the clay ball, two pause-and-think questions test what is always kept, and the clay ball is explained link by link. Then a worked example that tests if a collision is elastic, the exam trap about momentum in inelastic collisions, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.
